title: Toy Story 5 Lands in Indian Theatres This Friday. Taylor Swift Sings, Keanu Reeves Voices, and the Toys Are Fighting a Tablet.
excerpt: Pixar's most beloved franchise returns June 19 in 3D — and it's gunning straight for the Indian family audience in the same week Shahid Kapoor's 'A'-rated Cocktail 2 drops. History, as the trade keeps noting, is repeating itself.
body:
There is a generation of NRI kids who learned English partly from **Woody and Buzz** — who quoted "To infinity and beyond!" in playgrounds from Edison to Hounslow, who cried at the end of *Toy Story 3* in a college dorm far from home. That generation now has children of its own. And on **June 19**, Pixar is handing them a reason to take those kids to the cinema.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=c51ND9Hdbw0</youtube>

**Toy Story 5** releases in Indian theatres this Friday in 3D, and the premise lands with uncomfortable precision in 2026: the toys are at war with a screen. When eight-year-old Bonnie becomes attached to a sleek new tablet called **Lilypad** — voiced by **Greta Lee** with all the disruptive confidence of a piece of tech that's decided it knows what's best for your kid — Woody, Buzz, Jessie and the gang find themselves competing with digital glow for a child's attention. It is, depending on which critic you ask, either the most topical thing Pixar has done in years or a franchise gently restating what it already said beautifully.

The voice cast is a parade. **Tom Hanks** is back as Woody. **Tim Allen** returns as Buzz. **Joan Cusack**'s Jessie — a fan favourite since 1999 — gets her biggest role yet, and the film's emotional spine is built around her. And then the surprises: **Keanu Reeves**, **Conan O'Brien**, **Craig Robinson**, and **Bad Bunny** join the toy box. Directed by **Andrew Stanton** and co-directed by **McKenna Harris**, the film runs a tight 102 minutes.

Then there's the music. **Taylor Swift** performs the film's title song, *I Knew It, I Knew You*, written for Jessie's arc across the series — and at the film's premiere, Swift surprised fans by showing up and singing both the new track and the franchise's eternal anthem, *You've Got a Friend in Me*. For a Pixar premiere, that is the kind of A-list firepower that usually belongs to a Marvel finale.

The reviews are warm but not worshipful. *People* rounded up critics calling it "topical" and "sublime," while *The Independent*'s Clarisse Loughrey delivered the sting of the cycle, writing that the intended emotional punch "manages but a light slap" and calling it "the worst in the series" — even while admitting it's "a perfectly lovely film." The Daily Beast's Nick Schager landed somewhere kinder: "unnecessary and charming," with enough waterworks to justify the ticket.

> "Spending another 102 minutes with these CGI icons is never less than pleasurable, suggesting that though their story has long been complete, they're anything but obsolete." — Nick Schager, The Daily Beast

For the Indian market, the timing is the real drama. Toy Story 5 collides with **Cocktail 2** — Shahid Kapoor, Kriti Sanon and Rashmika Mandanna's 'A'-rated relationship saga — in the exact same release window. As Bollywood Hungama noted, history is repeating: an 'A'-rated Shahid Kapoor film clashing with a Disney-Pixar family juggernaut in the third week of June. The two films aren't fighting for the same seats — one is for date night, the other for the school-holiday crowd — but they are fighting for screens, and June 2026 has become Bollywood's most brutally crowded month in memory, with **nine major releases and over ₹1,400 crore at stake**.

The diaspora angle is the easy part. Toy Story 5 opens **day-and-date worldwide**, which means a family in San Jose, Toronto or Leicester walks into the same Friday-night 3D show as a family in Mumbai — no waiting weeks for an international release, no piracy temptation. In India it's English-language and 3D; abroad it's wherever your nearest multiplex is. Disney even pre-emptively adjusted the film to protect its China box office, a reminder of just how globally the studio is thinking.

Whether or not it's the best Toy Story — and it almost certainly isn't — there's something undeniable about a 31-year-old franchise still pulling Taylor Swift to its premiere and still making grown adults reach for tissues. The toys have always been a story about being loved, then outgrown, then loved again. Handing that story to a new set of kids, in a theatre, away from the tablet the film itself is warning them about? That's the most Pixar move imaginable.
